questions.q: What is the main difference between the SDLC and the SSDLC?
options: The SSDLC removes the testing stage entirely
The SSDLC layers a security activity onto every existing stage instead of adding one gate at the end
The SSDLC only applies to mobile applications
There is no difference — the terms are interchangeable
questions.explain: The Secure SDLC overlays a security activity onto each stage of the traditional SDLC (plan, design, develop, test, deploy, operate) rather than treating security as one final checkpoint.

questions.q: In the SSDLC, which stage is threat modeling typically performed at?
options: Operate/Maintain
Design
Release
Deploy
questions.explain: Threat modeling the architecture happens at the Design stage, before code is written — consistent with the shift-left principle from Lesson 1.

questions.q: At Northbridge Retail, automated SAST scans, dependency checks, and secrets scans on every pull request belong to which SSDLC stage?
options: Plan
Build/Test
Operate/Maintain
Design
questions.explain: Automated security testing in the pipeline — SAST, dependency scanning, secrets detection — runs during the Build/Test stage on every change.

questions.q: Why can't a single SSDLC stage substitute for the others?
options: Because each stage's security activity catches a different kind of problem that the others miss
Because only the Deploy stage has any real security value
Because the Plan stage automatically fixes all later vulnerabilities
Because stages must be completed in reverse order
questions.explain: A threat model won't catch a leaked dependency vulnerability, and a dependency scan won't catch an architectural flaw — each stage's activity addresses a distinct category of risk.

questions.q: Why does the lesson describe SSDLC security activities as cumulative rather than a one-time checklist?
options: Because every new pull request restarts the cycle at Develop and Build/Test, even for a feature that was planned and designed only once
Because security activities only need to happen during the original planning meeting
Because the SSDLC is only followed during a company's first year of operation
Because automated scans replace the need for a design-stage threat model
questions.explain: Security activities recur on every change — a new pull request re-triggers Develop and Build/Test stage checks even when Plan and Design happened once for the original feature.
